full_judgment:
The Government was the owner of the disputed land under District: Sylhet, Police Station: Kotwali, Mouza-Hajirai, JL No. 103, Khatian No. 1, SA Plot No. 177, subsequently the said plot was converted in to Plot No. 177/1 and Plot No. 177/2. One Moyna Miah, son of late Joyfor, of Hajirai, Police Station: Kotwali, District: Sylhet, applied for permanent settlement of Plot No. 177/1 measuring 3.37 acres before the then SDO Sylhet. The SDO on behalf of the Government, granted lease under a deed of lease being No. 2274/1974 to said Moyna Miah for a term of 10 (ten) years commencing from 1363 BS which would expire on 1372 BS on terms stipulated in the said deed. 

 3. Moyna Miah after 10 (ten) years i.e. on 11-1-1977 vide a registered deed being No. 26265 sold 1.87 acres of land out of 3.37 acres of land to one Abdul Mannan and handed over possession to him. Said Abdul Mannan on 6-6-1989 vide registered deed No. 7395 sold 1.80 acres of land to Noor Miah, Kudrat Miah and Kabir Miah; thereafter Md Moyna Miah again sold 1.20 acres of land to Md Tozummul Ali alias Tomzid Ali on 31-3-1982 vide registered deed No. 13536 and handed over possession to him. Md Tozummul Ali alias Tomzid Ali on 21-7-1985 vide registered deed No. 20026 sold 0.60 acres of land to Md Kudrat Miah and handed over possession. Subsequently, Noor Miah, Kudrat Miah and Kabir Miah sold 2.40 acres of land to the petitioner Nos.1 and 2 namely, Most. Salchabin Akhter and Most. Tasnim Akhter alias Taslim Akhter on 30-3-2003 vide registered deed No. 12786 and possession was handed over to them. Thereafter, the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 mutated their names vide Mutation Case No. 4752/2006-07 and paid rent to the Government till 1420 BS The petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 got Tosdik Math Porcha in their names under DP Khatian No. 232 but the respondent Nos. 7-9 have successfully managed the field officer to published their names in Math Porcha, the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 filed appeal being Appeal Case Nos. 45-48 of 2008 before the Assistant Settlement Officer against said Math Porcha, which are pending for hearing. 

 6. The respondent Nos. 7-9 claimed that they have purchased 3.37 acres of land from Moyna Miah vide three registered deeds being Nos. 12879, 12880 and 10481 on 19-9-1990, 19-9-1990 and 24-7-1990. After purchase they mutated their names and Khatian Nos. 575, 576 and 572/1 were prepared in their names and they paid rents. 

 10. Respondent Nos. 7-9, contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition contending inter-alia that one Moyna Mia was the owner and possessor of 3.37 acres of land by way of taking lease from the Government vide registered lease deed bearing number 2274 dated 5-2-1974 by creating a new bata dag (Plot) 177/1 and transferred the same in favour of respondent Nos. 7-9 by registered sale deed Nos. 12879, 12880 and 10481 dated 19-9-1990, 19-9-1990 and 24-7-1990 respectively. Accordingly, the said land was mutated in the names of respondent Nos. 7-9 under khatian Nos. 575, 576 and 572/1 and creating separate holding, the said respondents had been possessing the land on payment of rent and in the ongoing survey their names were recorded in DP khatian Nos. 628 and 490 against the said land of Plot No. 177/1 and they had been possessing the same for last 24/25 years till the lands were acquired. The subsequent mutation of the said land in the name of Moina Mia on 5-6-2003 in Mutation Case No. 6751/02-03 in khatian No. 736 was completely false, collusive and fabricated; since the writ petitioners claimed that Moina Mia disposed of the entire land of Plot No. 177/1 much before the date on which it was mutated in his name and therefore, subsequent mutation in the names of the writ petitioners in respect of the land purchased from Moina Mia also void, false and concocted. The deeds stated in the writ petition are also created and never acted upon. No so called predecessor in interest of the writ petitioners had mutated the land in his or her name. No transfer of possession of the land of Plot No. 177/1 took place in favour of the so called predecessors in interest of the writ petitioners or in their favour. Therefore, the writ petitioners do not have any locus standi to get compensation for the land of Plot No. 177/1.
